Every device added or removed be written into a logbook that can only be added t’, never edited or erased. Yer devices read it on every start, so a device ye did not add can’t appear here quietly - ye get told, an’ th’ entry stays in th’ book. Arrr.
Every direct message be encrypted, always, an’ that part can’t be switched off. This setting be about how carefully th’ other person\'s lock be checked before yer messages be sent t’ it. Arrr.
Every message already in yer encrypted conversations becomes permanently unreadable - by ye, by us, by anyone. Nothing brings ’em back. Arrr.

Not in th’ same room? Ye shall each see th’ same short row o’ numbers, called a safety code. Have ’em read it out on a phone call, or send it over another app ye already trust, an’ type it into th’ box under th’ code - th’ app compares all sixty digits, which be more than anyone manages by eye. If it matches, nobody be in th’ middle. Th’ one thing that doesn’t count be an OrangChat voice call - that audio goes through th’ same servers this check exists t’ test.

Send straight away - a swap gets caught. Every lock anyone publishes be written into a logbook that can only be added t’, never edited or erased. A swap can be attempted; it can’t be attempted quietly. Arrr.
Sending straight away be what every conversation gets. Checking first be th’ extra step, an’ it be only worth turning on fer folk ye can realistically meet or ring. Arrr.

Yer phone an’ yer computer each make their own key, on th’ device itself, th’ first time ye use encryption there. It goes into th’ part o’ th’ device built t’ guard keys, an’ it be made so that it can’t be read back out - not by OrangChat, not by another app, not by ye. There be nothing t’ leak an’ nothing t’ hand over.
Yer phone puts th’ message in a box an’ locks it. Every device in th’ conversation, an’ only those, holds a key t’ that box. Our servers store an’ pass along th’ locked box. Arrr.
